summary: Establish self-service Slack channel provisioning gateway with approval bot and scheduled archival
description: Issue summary: The Platform & Ops guild requests a self-service channel creation gateway for the Redwood Slack workspace to reduce manual ticket load and enforce naming, RBAC and archival policies. Impact: Currently Support handles ~30 channel creation requests / month; manual approvals create a backlog and inconsistent retention settings. Request: build an automated flow (Slack Workflow or bot) that validates requests, triggers a single approver based on team mappings, provisions channels with templates and metadata, and schedules archival reminders/auto-archive.
business_justification: Reduce operational load on Internal Support by ~70% for channel provisioning, improve channel discoverability via enforced naming/metadata, and reduce channel sprawl with automated archival. This ties to the org goal of standardizing project onboarding workflows and minimizing manual admin toil.
requirements: 1) Self-service form accessible to all employees (Slack shortcut or web). 2) Must attach a Jira project or Confluence space (optional but preferred). 3) Enforce naming prefixes per team mapping (e.g., eng-, data-, legal-). 4) Approval routing: single approver from mapped approver group; fallback to #ops if no approver. 5) Template content: pinned onboarding message, readme link to Confluence template, pre-populated channel purpose and topic. 6) Audit log stored in Confluence page and a dedicated #channel-provisioning log channel. 7) Automated archival reminder at 90 days of inactivity; auto-archive at 120 days unless renewed. 8) Must support private/public channel option. 9) Respect workspace admin permission model; app should not require owner-level tokens if avoidable.
acceptance_criteria: - Ability to create channel via Slack shortcut end-to-end without Support intervention. - Created channels follow naming conventions and include pinned onboarding message. - Approver receives a single interactive approval message and can approve/deny within Slack. - Audit entries appear in #channel-provisioning and a Confluence log page. - Archival reminders sent at 90 days; auto-archive at 120 days in test workspace. - Security review signoff from InfoSec confirming least privilege installation.
proposed_design: Option A: Use a lightweight ops bot (ops-channel-provisioner) hosted in k8s that receives Slack events, validates input, calls Slack admin API to create channel, sets topic/purpose, pins onboarding message, posts audit to #channel-provisioning and updates Confluence via API. Approval handled via interactive message to approver group. Option B: Use Slack Workflow Builder + a lightweight webhook for approval and API calls. Preference: Option A for better RBAC control and visibility. Implementation to follow PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-tools/pull/812 for the bot framework.
security_considerations: - App should request minimum scopes: channels:manage, chat:write, users:read, conversations:read, admin (if required for private channels). - Prefer installing as a workspace app with granular installation by workspace admin. - All actions must be logged; sensitive tokens stored in KMS. - Approval groups should be mapped to Okta group sync; fallback approver must be minimal. - Risk: abusive channel creation; mitigate with rate limiting and quota per user/team.
rollout_plan: 1) Build bot in dev workspace and run a small pilot with two pods (Platform & Data). 2) Security review + token storage validated. 3) Pilot phase (2 weeks) with telemetry: # requests, approval times, failed creations. 4) Adjust naming rules and archival cadence per pilot feedback. 5) Full workspace rollout and deprecation of manual ticket form. 6) Post-rollout audit at 30 days.
